draft.title: Fission and fusion
card: A heavy nucleus, such as uranium, splits into smaller nuclei. Nuclear power stations use fission, and they leave radioactive waste that must be stored safely.
Light nuclei, such as hydrogen, join to form a heavier nucleus. Fusion is how the Sun releases energy.
Both reactions change the nucleus, not just the outer electrons. This is why they release huge amounts of energy compared with chemical reactions.
To tell them apart, ask what happens to the nucleus. If one big nucleus breaks into smaller ones, it is fission. If small nuclei combine into a bigger one, it is fusion.
draft.remember: Fission splits a heavy nucleus. Fusion joins light nuclei. Both release huge amounts of energy.

a.q: Which description matches a nuclear fission reaction?
opts: A uranium nucleus splits into smaller nuclei
Two hydrogen nuclei join to form a helium nucleus
A nucleus gains electrons to form a negative ion
Two atoms share electrons to form a molecule
a.why: Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus such as uranium into smaller nuclei. Two hydrogen nuclei joining is fusion, which is the most tempting wrong option because it is also a nuclear reaction.

b.q: Dr Lee compares two reactions. In Reaction X, a large nucleus breaks into two smaller ones. In Reaction Y, small nuclei combine into a larger one. Which statement is correct?
opts: X is used in power stations and Y happens in the Sun
Y is used in power stations and X happens in the Sun
X releases energy but Y does not release any
X and Y both leave no radioactive waste at all
b.why: X is fission, which nuclear power stations use, and Y is fusion, which powers the Sun. The swapped option is tempting but reverses the two reactions. Both release huge amounts of energy, so the option saying only one does is wrong.
b.clue: Work out which reaction splits and which joins.

a.best: A uranium nucleus splits into smaller nuclei

b.best: X is used in power stations and Y happens in the Sun
